findings.detail: The new dev-branch lane builds, signs (the same Developer ID signature as master), notarizes and registers every push to `dev`. The registered build is a trusted official-build identity on the dev coordinator (`require_app_attest_qualification=true`). The doc says review is not enforced on `dev` today, and that only the "Darkbloom PR access control" bypass-list accounts can push. It defers the fix to a pull_request rule that an administrator adds later. The lane also calls the reusable workflow with `secrets: inherit`, which exposes every repository secret, including `PROD_*` and `STAGING_*`. Only a test pins the guards that keep those secrets from being read. A single bypass-list account, or a compromised one, could ship unreviewed code that is notarized and registered as a trusted build. A change to the reusable workflow could also read production secrets. The threat model does not cover this release-signing path (A-005, A-011, T-013, T-034). Fix: land the pull_request/CODEOWNERS rule before enabling the lane, and pass only the named secrets instead of using `secrets: inherit`. Record the dev signing path in the threat model.
findings.title: Documented dev-branch lane signs unreviewed code with the production Developer ID, with the review rule not yet enforced

findings.detail: The new `cluster_runtime` block makes a coordinator derive pair approvals, pair-serving grants and public parity qualifications from every signed release. The docs say these qualifications apply to the whole mode family "on any Apple silicon pair", and that the declared placement names the evidence rather than limiting traffic. They also admit that no pipeline of either model ran on two M5 Ultras and that GLM has no tensor-parallel cross-cable record. The admission rests on an owner decision, not on tested placements. Public consumer prompts (A-001) are then split across two provider Macs, and intermediate activations cross a LAN link between them. Neither the retained TB-002/TB-007 text nor T-007 and T-056 addresses the confidentiality of that inter-member link, the trust placed in the second provider, or the correctness of unqualified placements. Both providers are adversarial in this model. A malicious member pair could see or alter traffic that no single-provider guarantee covers. Fix: bind qualifications to the tested numerics classes and placements, and add a threat-model entry for cluster routing that covers member trust and the inter-member channel before public routing is enabled.
findings.title: Release-derived public cluster qualifications admit consumer traffic on unqualified placements; the threat model does not cover cluster routing

findings.detail: parityQualifications() (ClusterRuntimeApprovalFacts.swift:331-333) hardcodes promotable:true, diverged:false, a constant evidenceSHA256 and a constant qualifiedAt (ClusterPublicModels.swift:46-48). It derives the numerics class from whatever metallib the release ships, combined with the hardcoded 'applegpu_g17d'/macOS 27.0 ranks. Any build whose worker reports the two declared artifact hashes is therefore emitted as parity-qualified for public traffic with a 1M-token envelope. This holds even if the metallib, worker or placement code changed since the 2026-10-31 evidence run. Nothing in the facts ties the qualification to the evidence run's build or digests. The evidence digest is also not the records digest used for non-declared grants (evidenceSHA256()). The only link is a test that the constant equals the hash of a doc. A coordinator that derives approvals from these facts (outside the supplied evidence) will treat the claim as qualification. Impact: a regressed or divergent numerics build can be admitted to serve public consumers. Fix: bind the qualification to the qualified metallib/worker/placement digests, or require the coordinator to check them against allowlisted evidence-run digests. Re-run the parity evidence on metallib changes.
findings.title: Public-traffic parity qualifications are asserted from compile-time constants for any build, not bound to evidence for that build

findings.detail: provider-release.md head 653-668 says each signed release can carry `cluster_runtime` in `POST /v1/releases`. An accepting coordinator derives that build's cluster approvals, pair-serving grants and public parity qualifications from it, and no operator posts them per build. The block comes from the release's own CLI/worker (`--list-release-models`, `--describe-runtime`) and from catalog/CDN data fetched at build time (head ~689-713). Qualifications apply to each declared family on any Apple silicon pair, not only the evidenced placement (head 662-666). This merges release publication with qualification authority. A-017/T-054 treat durable build qualification as independently approved and separate from release publication. A holder of the release key or the CI lane, or a build whose self-declared `ClusterPublicModels` or qualification records are wrong, can enable public pair serving without separate approval. No threat-model boundary, asset or threat covers cluster pair grants or public cluster routing. The coordinator-side consumers (ParseReleaseClusterRuntime, NativeRuntimeCatalogWithReleases) and the scripts are not in the supplied evidence. Fix: add a TB/threat entry for release-derived cluster approvals. State whether release-key compromise now implies public cluster qualification, keep an independent approval step or a per-environment switch bound to platform review, and record the any-pair broadening and catalog-eviction behavior (64/64/256 bounds).
findings.title: Release registration now self-derives cluster grants and public qualifications outside the modeled independent-qualification boundary

findings.detail:
Head lines 653-668 and 715-750 say a signed release's POST /v1/releases payload can carry `cluster_runtime`. A coordinator that accepts it derives build-pinned cluster approvals, pair-serving grants and promotable parity qualifications for public traffic. "No operator posts approvals, grants or public qualifications per build" (head 662). Before this change, a person copied these facts into the operator approval file.

The release key (A-005) and the CI pipeline now carry routing and public-traffic authority on top of binary/build identity (A-011, A-017). The payload content comes from the built app's own CLI (`env -i`, keychain removed first, head 675-684) and from fetched catalog/CDN `input_modalities`, which widen the media envelope (head 702-704).

Per head 663-666, a qualification applies to any Apple silicon pair regardless of numerics class. For GLM-5.3-Flash and Qwen3.8-27B this rests on an owner decision, not on recorded parity. The dev lane (head 527-531) has no enforced review yet still registers with DEV_RELEASE_KEY. On DevNet, an unreviewed dev push with DEV_CLUSTER_RUNTIME_ENABLED=true can therefore change public cluster routing.

TB-002, T-007, T-054 and A-018 do not describe cluster pairs, derived approvals or this authority path. Fix: add a cluster-runtime boundary or threat covering derivation from release payloads, catalog-sourced envelopes and the any-pair promotion policy. Require dev review before enabling the variable, and verify that the platform's strict parsing and catalog bounds back these docs.
findings.title: Release registration now authors cluster approvals and public-traffic qualifications; the threat model has no entry for this
